Chiral Box-Copper/Zinc Catalysts
Ni Zhao, Shuai-Ru Cheng, Hui-Juan Ma, Wei-Wei Zhang, Guo-rong Ma, and Pei Wang*
ABSTRACT: A method for the asymmetric propargylation and allenylation of isatins catalyzed using chiral Box-copper/zinc
catalysts is described. By modulation of the metal and solvent, a series of chiral 3-hydroxy-3-propargyl-2-oxindoles and 3-hydroxy-3-
allenyl-2-oxindoles are selectively synthesized in good yields with excellent enantio- and regioselectivities.

Notably, electron-withdrawing groups at the C7 position
resulted in particularly good yields and ee values (entries 6−9).
When 7-methylisatin was used as a substrate, the yield and ee
value significantly decreased, which may be due to the
electronic properties of the methyl group (entry 10). For
disubstituted isatins, 5,6-difluoroisatin gave the target product
with a higher yield and ee value, whereas 4-chloro-5-
fluoroisatin exhibited the lowest enantioselectivity (69% ee)
(entries 11−12). Substitution at the N1 position with methyl,
phenyl, or benzyl groups gave better enantioselectivity, and a
methyl substituent at N1 position gave the best result with an
ee up to 95% (entries 13−15). Similarly, 5-substituted
methylisatins also furnished good results (entries 16−17).
Fortunately, high regioselectivities were obtained in all cases.
Various substituted isatins were then reacted with allenyl
boronate 3 under the optimized conditions (Table 3).
Regardless of the presence or absence of a protecting group
on the N atom of isatin, the reaction proceeded smoothly to
aford the allenyl alcohols 5a−q in excellent yields and
selectivities. Isatins bearing electron-withdrawing groups such
as F, Cl, Br, and

According to previous literature reports,<sup>16</sup> a probable
mechanism is illustrated in Scheme 2. Initially, a metal−
boron exchange reaction occurs between allenylboronic acid
pinacol esters and IA/IB, forming propargyl spieces IIA and
IIB. Due to the low energy barrier for isomerization between
IIA and its isomer IIA′, rapid isomerization can occur. The
addition reaction between IIA′ and 2a proceeds more rapidly,
leading to the formation of propargyl alcohol product 4a. In
contrast, IIB does not undergo significant isomerization and
complexes with istain 2a to form intermediate IIIB.
Subsequently, the zinc-propargyl complex attack of the
carbonyl group isolates 2a from the Re-face. This hypothesis

of the reaction intermediates.

propargylation and allenylation of isatin derivatives using a
commercially available organoboron reagent under Box-Cu/Zn
catalysis. The reaction conditions are well-tolerated by both
protected and unprotected isatins, yielding a series of propargyl
and allenyl tertiary alcohols in moderate to high yields with
excellent enantio- and regioselectivities. Notably, the ee value
of propargyl alcohol reached 95%, surpassing that of the
SEGPHOS-Cu(II) catalytic system reported previously. The

mechanism is illustrated in Scheme 2. Initially, a metal−
boron exchange reaction occurs between allenylboronic acid
pinacol esters and IA/IB, forming propargyl spieces IIA and

IIA and its isomer IIA′, rapid isomerization can occur. The
addition reaction between IIA′ and 2a proceeds more rapidly,
leading to the formation of propargyl alcohol product 4a. In
contrast, IIB does not undergo significant isomerization and
complexes with istain 2a to form intermediate IIIB.
Subsequently, the zinc-propargyl complex attack of the
carbonyl group isolates 2a from the Re-face. This hypothesis

the Supporting Information).

and allenyl tertiary alcohols in moderate to high yields with
